questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in which year?
questions.explanation: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 was passed by Parliament on 5 August 2019. '2020' is wrong. '2018' is wrong. '2017' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the rivers of J&K:

(i) The Jhelum originates from Verinag spring in Anantnag.
(ii) The Chenab is formed by the confluence of Chandra and Bhaga rivers.
(iii) The Tawi is a tributary of the Jhelum.
(iv) The Indus enters J&K/Ladakh from Tibet.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Jhelum from Verinag (i-correct). Chenab = Chandra+Bhaga (ii-correct). Indus enters from Tibet (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — Tawi is a tributary of the Chenab, not Jhelum.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Akhnoor Fort in Jammu is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Akhnoor Fort sits on the banks of the Chenab river. 'Tawi' flows through Jammu city but not at Akhnoor. 'Jhelum' is in Kashmir Valley. 'Ravi' barely touches J&K's border.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Kashmir Valley is known as the 'Paradise on Earth'.
Reason (R): The Valley is surrounded by mountains, has a temperate climate, and is dotted with lakes, gardens, and scenic meadows.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Kashmir is called Paradise on Earth (A-correct). Its natural beauty with mountains, climate, lakes and gardens is the reason for this name (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K districts with their administrative divisions:

Column I:
(a) Poonch
(b) Baramulla
(c) Doda
(d) Pulwama

Column II:
(i) Kashmir Division
(ii) Jammu Division
(iii) Kashmir Division
(iv) Jammu Division

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Poonch is in Jammu Division (ii). Baramulla is in Kashmir Division (i). Doda is in Jammu Division (iv). Pulwama is in Kashmir Division (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Shalimar Bagh in Srinagar was originally built by Mughal Emperor:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh was built by Emperor Jahangir in 1619 for his wife Nur Jahan. 'Akbar' built the Hari Parbat fort wall. 'Shah Jahan' expanded/modified it later. 'Aurangzeb' did not build gardens in Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are official languages of the UT of J&K under the J&K Official Languages Act, 2020?

(i) Kashmiri
(ii) Dogri
(iii) Hindi
(iv) Urdu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The J&K Official Languages Act, 2020 recognizes Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, and English as official languages. All four listed are included.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dulhasti Power Station on the Chenab River has an installed capacity of:
questions.explanation: Dulhasti HEP on the Chenab has 390 MW installed capacity. '480 MW' is Uri-I. '690 MW' is Salal. '330 MW' is Kishanganga.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the history of J&K:

(i) The Treaty of Amritsar (1846) transferred Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
(ii) Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah became the first Prime Minister of J&K.
(iii) The Instrument of Accession was signed on 26 October 1947.
(iv) J&K had its own separate constitution adopted in 1965.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Treaty of Amritsar gave Kashmir to Gulab Singh (i-correct). Sheikh Abdullah was first PM (ii-correct). IoA signed 26 Oct 1947 (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — J&K Constitution was adopted on 17 November 1956, not 1965.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Saffron is called 'Red Gold' in J&K.
Reason (R): Saffron is extremely expensive due to the labour-intensive harvesting process and limited growing areas.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Saffron is called Red Gold (A-correct). Its high cost due to labour-intensive harvesting explains the 'gold' comparison (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Martand Sun Temple ruins near Anantnag were built during which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Martand Sun Temple was built by Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty (8th century). 'Lohara' came later (11th-12th century). 'Mughal' arrived in 16th century. 'Dogra' ruled from 1846.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following power projects with their installed capacities:

Column I:
(a) Salal HEP
(b) Uri-I HEP
(c) Kishanganga HEP
(d) Baglihar HEP (Stage I & II)

Column II:
(i) 330 MW
(ii) 690 MW
(iii) 480 MW
(iv) 450 MW

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Salal = 690 MW (ii). Uri-I = 480 MW (iii). Kishanganga = 330 MW (i). Baglihar I+II = 450 MW (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Nund Rishi' shrine at Charar-i-Sharief is in which district?
questions.explanation: Charar-i-Sharief (shrine of Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani/Nund Rishi) is in Budgam district. 'Srinagar' is wrong. 'Baramulla' is wrong. 'Ganderbal' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the RTI Act in J&K:

(i) After 2019 reorganization, the central RTI Act, 2005 became applicable to J&K.
(ii) An RTI application fee is ₹10 under the central Act.
(iii) Information must be provided within 30 days.
(iv) The Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Minister.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Central RTI Act applied post-2019 (i-correct). Fee is ₹10 (ii-correct). 30-day time limit (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — CIC is appointed by the President on recommendation of a committee headed by the PM.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which pass connects the Kishtwar area to the Zanskar valley?
questions.explanation: Umasi La (5,342m) connects Kishtwar to Zanskar. 'Zoji La' connects Kashmir to Ladakh. 'Banihal Pass' connects Kashmir to Jammu. 'Sinthan Top' connects Anantnag to Kishtwar/Breng Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Mughal Road is considered an alternative to the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway.
Reason (R): The Mughal Road connects Shopian (Kashmir) to Rajouri-Poonch (Jammu), bypassing the congested Banihal-Qazigund route.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Mughal Road is an alternative route (A-correct). Its connection between Shopian and Rajouri/Poonch bypassing NH-44 explains its role as an alternative (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Habba Khatoon' of Kashmir is remembered primarily as:
options: A renowned poetess of the 16th century
The first woman ruler of Kashmir
A freedom fighter against Dogra rule
A religious reformer of the 14th century
questions.correctAnswer: A renowned poetess of the 16th century
questions.explanation: Habba Khatoon was a 16th century Kashmiri poetess known as the 'Nightingale of Kashmir'. 'First woman ruler' was Didda. 'Freedom fighter' is wrong. 'Religious reformer' describes Nund Rishi/Lal Ded.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following districts are in the Kashmir Division?

(i) Shopian
(ii) Kathua
(iii) Ganderbal
(iv) Kulgam

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Shopian (i), Ganderbal (iii), and Kulgam (iv) are in Kashmir Division. Kathua (ii) is in Jammu Division — it's the southernmost district of J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Banihal-Qazigund Road Tunnel (also called Navyug Tunnel) reduces travel distance between Jammu and Srinagar by approximately:
questions.explanation: The Banihal-Qazigund tunnel (opened 2021) reduces the distance by approximately 16 km and avoids the old Jawahar Tunnel route. '30 km' is too high. '5 km' is too low. '25 km' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist destinations with their descriptions:

Column I:
(a) Pahalgam
(b) Sonamarg
(c) Patnitop
(d) Bhaderwah

Column II:
(i) 'Mini Kashmir' of Jammu
(ii) 'Meadow of Gold'
(iii) 'Valley of Shepherds'
(iv) Hill station on NH-44 near Batote

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Pahalgam = Valley of Shepherds (iii). Sonamarg = Meadow of Gold (ii). Patnitop = hill station on NH-44 (iv). Bhaderwah = Mini Kashmir (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The first railway line in J&K (Jammu-Udhampur section) was inaugurated in which year?
questions.explanation: The Jammu-Udhampur rail section (53 km) was inaugurated in April 2005. '2000' is wrong. '2008' is wrong. '2003' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indus Waters Treaty:

(i) It was signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan.
(ii) It was brokered by the World Bank.
(iii) India received exclusive rights over the Jhelum River.
(iv) The eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) were allocated to India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Signed 1960 (i-correct). Brokered by World Bank (ii-correct). Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — Jhelum is a WESTERN river allocated to Pakistan (India has limited use rights).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Apple cultivation in J&K is concentrated in the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The temperate climate with cold winters and moderate summers, along with well-drained Karewa soils, provides ideal conditions for apple orchards.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Apple cultivation is mainly in Kashmir Valley (A-correct). Temperate climate and Karewa soils directly explain suitability (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Dogri' language belongs to which language family?
questions.explanation: Dogri is an Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the Jammu region. 'Dravidian' includes Tamil, Telugu etc. 'Sino-Tibetan' includes Ladakhi/Tibetan. 'Austroasiatic' includes Santali, Mundari etc.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are GI-tagged products of J&K?

(i) Kashmir Pashmina
(ii) Kashmir Saffron
(iii) Kani Shawl
(iv) Basmati Rice (Punjab/Haryana)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Kashmir Pashmina (i), Kashmir Saffron (ii), and Kani Shawl (iii) all have GI tags from J&K. (iv) is wrong — Basmati Rice GI is associated with Punjab/Haryana/UP, not J&K specifically.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following rulers/personalities with their contributions to J&K:

Column I:
(a) Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah)
(b) Maharaja Ranbir Singh
(c) Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
(d) Maharaja Gulab Singh

Column II:
(i) Established Dogra rule through Treaty of Amritsar
(ii) Known as 'Sher-e-Kashmir', led Naya Kashmir movement
(iii) Promoted Sanskrit learning and built Raghunath Temple
(iv) Golden period of Kashmir — promoted arts, abolished jizya

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Budshah = Golden era, arts, abolished jizya (iv). Ranbir Singh = Sanskrit, Raghunath Temple (iii). Sheikh Abdullah = Sher-e-Kashmir, Naya Kashmir (ii). Gulab Singh = Treaty of Amritsar (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hemis Festival in Ladakh celebrates the birthday of:
questions.explanation: Hemis Festival celebrates the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava who introduced Buddhism to Tibet. 'Buddha' is celebrated on Buddha Purnima. 'Dalai Lama' is not related to Hemis. 'Adi Shankaracharya' was a Hindu philosopher.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the handicrafts of J&K:

(i) Pashmina wool comes from the Changthangi goat of Ladakh.
(ii) Papier-mâché is a craft involving decorated paper pulp objects.
(iii) Khatamband is intricate walnut wood furniture carving.
(iv) Namda is a type of felted woollen rug.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Pashmina from Changthangi goat (i-correct). Papier-mâché = decorated paper pulp (ii-correct). Namda = felted wool rug (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — Khatamband is ceiling woodwork with interlocking pieces (not walnut furniture carving; walnut carving is a separate craft).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pangong Tso lake shared between India and China is situated at an altitude of approximately:
questions.explanation: Pangong Tso is at approximately 4,350m (14,270 ft) altitude in eastern Ladakh. '3,500m' is too low. '5,200m' is too high (that's near Everest base camp). '2,800m' is too low.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in India.
Reason (R): The tunnel is approximately 11.2 km long and is part of the USBRL project connecting Banihal to Qazigund.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: It is India's longest railway tunnel (A-correct). Its 11.2 km length as part of USBRL explains this distinction (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following wildlife sanctuaries/national parks are in J&K?

(i) Dachigam National Park
(ii) Kishtwar National Park
(iii) Hemis National Park
(iv) Salim Ali National Park

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Dachigam NP (i-correct, near Srinagar). Kishtwar NP (ii-correct, in Kishtwar district). Salim Ali NP (iv-correct, in Srinagar, near Dal Lake). Hemis NP (iii) is in LADAKH UT, not J&K UT.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Bahu Fort' in Jammu, one of the oldest structures in the city, is dedicated to:
questions.explanation: Bahu Fort houses the temple of Goddess Kali (Bawe Wali Mata), a revered deity in Jammu. 'Lord Shiva' is wrong. 'Guru Nanak Dev' is wrong. 'Lord Vishnu' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ Agreement of 1975 restored Sheikh Abdullah to power as Chief Minister of J&K.
questions.explanation: The Indira-Sheikh Accord (1975) ended Sheikh Abdullah's political exile and he became CM. 'Delhi' was the 1952 agreement. 'Shimla' was the 1972 India-Pakistan agreement. 'Kashmir' is not a named accord.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes of J&K with their locations:

Column I:
(a) Mansar Lake
(b) Dal Lake
(c) Wular Lake
(d) Manasbal Lake

Column II:
(i) Srinagar
(ii) Bandipora
(iii) Ganderbal
(iv) Udhampur

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Mansar Lake is in Udhampur district (iv). Dal Lake is in Srinagar (i). Wular Lake is in Bandipora (ii). Manasbal Lake is in Ganderbal (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Purple Revolution' or 'Aroma Mission' in J&K is associated with:
questions.explanation: The Purple Revolution promotes lavender cultivation in J&K (especially Doda, Bhaderwah). 'Saffron rejuvenation' is the National Saffron Mission. 'Apple high-density' is a separate scheme. 'Tulip farming' relates to the Tulip Garden.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the climate of Jammu region:

(i) It experiences a sub-tropical climate in the plains.
(ii) The monsoon brings significant rainfall in July-September.
(iii) Winters are as severe as in the Kashmir Valley.
(iv) The Shivalik Hills border the Jammu plains to the south.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Jammu plains have sub-tropical climate (i-correct). Monsoon brings heavy rain (ii-correct). Shivaliks border to the south (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — Jammu winters are much milder than Kashmir's freezing temperatures.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Ranbir Penal Code' was the criminal law applicable in J&K before its replacement. It was replaced by:
options: The J&K Criminal Procedure Code in 2010
questions.explanation: The Ranbir Penal Code (J&K's separate criminal law) was replaced by the IPC when J&K became a UT in 2019. 'British Criminal Code' is wrong. 'Sharia law' is wrong. 'J&K CrPC 2010' is fabricated.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Tourism is a major contributor to J&K's economy.
Reason (R): J&K attracts millions of pilgrims (Amarnath, Vaishno Devi) and recreational tourists (Dal Lake, Gulmarg, Pahalgam) annually.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Tourism is a major GDP contributor (A-correct). Pilgrim and recreational tourism drawing millions directly explains the economic contribution (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Nishat Bagh (Garden of Joy) in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: Nishat Bagh was built by Asif Khan (brother-in-law of Jahangir) in 1633. 'Jahangir' built Shalimar Bagh. 'Dara Shikoh' built Pari Mahal. 'Akbar' built the Hari Parbat fort wall.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following crops are grown in the Jammu region (plains)?

(i) Wheat
(ii) Basmati Rice
(iii) Saffron
(iv) Maize

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Wheat (i), Basmati Rice (ii — R.S. Pura belt), and Maize (iv) are Jammu plain crops. Saffron (iii) is grown in the Kashmir Valley (Pampore), not the Jammu plains.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the highest governing body of the Shri Amarnath Shrine, managing the annual yatra.
questions.explanation: SASB manages the Amarnath Yatra and shrine administration. 'Tourism Department' promotes tourism broadly. 'Home Ministry' handles security. 'Shrine Management Committee' is not the official name.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K personalities with their fields:

Column I:
(a) Agha Shahid Ali
(b) Habba Khatoon
(c) Maqbool Sherwani
(d) Major Somnath Sharma

Column II:
(i) First Param Vir Chakra recipient (1947)
(ii) National hero who delayed tribal raiders in Baramulla (1947)
(iii) Renowned Urdu/English poet
(iv) 16th century Kashmiri poetess

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Agha Shahid Ali = renowned poet (iii). Habba Khatoon = 16th century poetess (iv). Maqbool Sherwani = hero of 1947 (ii). Major Somnath Sharma = first PVC (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Basohli' paintings of J&K are famous for:
options: Miniature paintings depicting scenes from Hindu epics with bold colours
Landscape paintings of the Kashmir Valley
questions.correctAnswer: Miniature paintings depicting scenes from Hindu epics with bold colours
questions.explanation: Basohli miniatures (17th-18th century, Jammu region) are known for bold colours and Hindu epic themes. 'Landscape paintings' is wrong. 'Buddhist thangka' is from Ladakh. 'Mughal calligraphy' is unrelated to Basohli.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the DDC (District Development Council) elections in J&K:

(i) DDC elections were first held in December 2020.
(ii) Each district has 14 DDC constituencies.
(iii) DDC is the third tier of the Panchayati Raj system in J&K.
(iv) DDC members are directly elected by the public.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: First DDC elections in Dec 2020 (i-correct). 14 constituencies per district (ii-correct). DDC is the third tier (iii-correct). Members directly elected (iv-correct). All are correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Zabarwan Range, which forms the backdrop of Dal Lake, is a part of:
questions.explanation: Zabarwan is a short sub-range of the Lesser/Middle Himalayas bordering Srinagar. 'Greater Himalayas' are further north. 'Pir Panjal' is to the south of the Kashmir Valley. 'Shivaliks' are foothills near Jammu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Delimitation Commission increased J&K assembly seats from 87 to 90.
Reason (R): The delimitation was carried out to ensure better representation based on the 2011 Census population data.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Seats increased from 87 to 90 (A-correct). Census-based representation was the driving purpose (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Amar Mahal Palace' in Jammu was built in which architectural style?
questions.explanation: Amar Mahal was built in the French chateau style with red sandstone. 'Mughal style' characterizes gardens. 'Rajput style' is in Rajasthan. 'Gothic style' is European church architecture.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The traditional Kashmiri fire-pot used for personal warmth in winter is called a __________.
questions.explanation: The Kangri is an earthen pot filled with burning charcoal, carried under the pheran for warmth. 'Samovar' is a tea urn. 'Hamam' is a bath. 'Bukhari' is a room heater/stove.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tunnels with their routes:

Column I:
(a) Jawahar Tunnel
(b) Chenani-Nashri Tunnel
(c) Zoji La Tunnel (under construction)
(d) Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel

Column II:
(i) Sonmarg to Dras (Ladakh connection)
(ii) Banihal to Qazigund (old route)
(iii) Chenani to Nashri on NH-44
(iv) Banihal to Qazigund (railway)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jawahar Tunnel connects Banihal to Qazigund on old road (ii). Chenani-Nashri is on NH-44 (iii). Zoji La tunnel will connect Sonmarg to Dras (i). Pir Panjal tunnel is railway Banihal-Qazigund (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Shikara' boats of Kashmir are traditionally associated with which water body?
questions.explanation: Shikaras are most iconic on Dal Lake in Srinagar. While they exist on other Kashmir lakes too, Dal Lake is their primary association. 'Wular Lake' is mainly for fishing. 'Manasbal' is known for lotus. 'Pangong' is in Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the J&K economy:

(i) Horticulture (especially apple, walnut) is the backbone of Kashmir's economy.
(ii) J&K produces over 75% of India's total apple output.
(iii) Handicrafts like carpets and shawls generate significant export revenue.
(iv) Heavy industries dominate J&K's industrial sector.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Horticulture is Kashmir's backbone (i-correct). J&K produces 75%+ of India's apples (ii-correct). Handicrafts generate export revenue (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — J&K has very limited heavy industry; small-scale and cottage industries dominate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Dogra Art Museum' in Jammu houses collections related to:
questions.explanation: The Dogra Art Museum (Mubarak Mandi complex) primarily houses Pahari and Basohli miniature paintings. 'Modern art' is wrong. 'Buddhist sculptures' are in Ladakh. 'Mughal architecture' is in gardens.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The 'Back to Village' programme was launched in J&K after its reorganization.
Reason (R): The programme aims to strengthen grassroots democracy and improve delivery of government services at the village level.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: 'Back to Village' was launched post-reorganization (A-correct). Its aim of grassroots democracy and service delivery explains its purpose and existence (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kishtwar National Park is known for the conservation of which endangered animal?
questions.explanation: Kishtwar NP protects the endangered Himalayan Brown Bear. 'Snow Leopard' is associated with Hemis NP. 'Hangul' is in Dachigam NP. 'Markhor' is found in Pir Panjal but is not specifically associated with Kishtwar NP.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (river — its origin in J&K)?

(i) Jhelum — Verinag Spring
(ii) Lidder — Kolahoi Glacier
(iii) Sind — Machoi Glacier
(iv) Tawi — Zoji La

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Jhelum from Verinag (i-correct). Lidder from Kolahoi Glacier (ii-correct). Sind from Machoi Glacier near Sonamarg (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — Tawi originates from the Kali Kundi glacier in Pir Panjal, not Zoji La.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following festivals with their regions in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Baisakhi
(b) Shivratri (Herath)
(c) Lohri
(d) Eid-ul-Adha

Column II:
(i) Celebrated across J&K by Muslims
(ii) Major harvest festival in Jammu
(iii) Celebrated by Kashmiri Pandits
(iv) Dogra/Punjabi community in Jammu

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Baisakhi = harvest festival in Jammu (ii). Shivratri/Herath = Kashmiri Pandits' major festival (iii). Lohri = Dogra/Punjabi community (iv). Eid-ul-Adha = Muslims across J&K (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Tosa Maidan' meadow, a former military firing range returned to civilian use, is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Tosa Maidan is a high-altitude meadow in Budgam district that was returned from army use to civilians. 'Baramulla' is wrong. 'Bandipora' is wrong. 'Kupwara' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chenab Bridge (USBRL project):

(i) It is the world's highest railway arch bridge.
(ii) It spans the Chenab river in Reasi district.
(iii) Its deck height is approximately 359 metres above the river.
(iv) It is shorter than the Eiffel Tower.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: World's highest railway arch bridge (i-correct). Spans Chenab in Reasi (ii-correct). 359m deck height (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — at 359m, it is TALLER than the Eiffel Tower (330m), not shorter.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Chinar' tree, iconic to the Kashmir Valley, is scientifically known as:
questions.explanation: The Chinar (Oriental Plane tree) is Platanus orientalis. 'Cedrus deodara' is Deodar. 'Juglans regia' is Walnut. 'Salix alba' is Willow.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The J&K Police recruitment exam includes a section on 'General Knowledge with special reference to J&K'.
Reason (R): Knowledge of local geography, history, and current affairs is considered essential for policing duties within the Union Territory.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The exam includes a J&K GK section (A-correct). Local knowledge being essential for policing explains its inclusion (R-correct and explains A).
